attributes.verification_note: TWO DESIGN REVERSALS CAME FROM THE NEGATIVE HALF, and both would have shipped wrong without it. Item 5: a gate keyed on the scratch path alone refuses 7 fields and is wrong on 6 (86% false positives) — reading the would-be-refused SET rather than its size is what showed it, and the shipped discriminant is the FALLBACK, not the path. Item 9: ranking --asserted-by results by refusal language looked like the useful half until the non-matching rows were counted (17/17, 46/51, 19/20 carry necessity wording), so it is reported and ranked on nothing. A third, smaller reversal came from a live measurement: refreshing `last_bytes` in item 2's re-score traded one false banner for another (the next probe annotated its NEUTRAL as 'the edit FOLDED AWAY before codegen' about an edit that does not exist), so the field is dropped rather than refreshed.
